frame: Heliocentric inertial (HCI): solar equatorial plane, x towards the ascending node of the solar equator on the J2000 ecliptic (i = 7.25 deg, Omega = 75.76 deg).
source: JPL Horizons (ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api), geometric states about the Sun's centre.

objects.name: Solar Orbiter
objects.predictedNote: SolO: Horizons ephemeris to 2030-11-20, then a two-body propagation of its final state.
objects.note: Launched 2020-02-10. Horizons ephemeris 2020-02-11 to 2030-11-20. Extended to 2030-12-31: then a two-body propagation of its final state.

objects.name: Parker Solar Probe
objects.predictedNote: PSP: Horizons ephemeris to 2030-01-01, then a two-body propagation of its final state.
objects.note: Launched 2018-08-12. Horizons ephemeris 2018-08-13 to 2030-01-01. Extended to 2030-12-31: then a two-body propagation of its final state.

objects.name: L1 (Earth)
objects.note: Earth's position shifted 1.5 million km sunward to the L1 point. Horizons ephemeris 2018-01-01 to 2030-12-31.

objects.name: BepiColombo
objects.predictedNote: Bepi: Horizons ephemeris to 2027-04-11, then Mercury's position, by which time it is in orbit there.
objects.note: Launched 2018-10-20. Horizons ephemeris 2018-10-21 to 2027-04-11. Extended to 2030-12-31: then Mercury's position, by which time it is in orbit there.

objects.name: STEREO-A
objects.predictedNote: STA: Horizons ephemeris to 2026-12-18, then a two-body propagation of its final state.
objects.note: In free heliocentric drift. Horizons ephemeris 2018-01-01 to 2026-12-18. Extended to 2030-12-31: then a two-body propagation of its final state.
